newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Emergency medical supplies arrive in Zaire war zone.
newsitem.headline: Emergency medical supplies arrive in Zaire war zone.

text.p: Emergency medical supplies arrived in the east Zaire city of Goma on Saturday for the first time since battles erupted more than a week ago and have killed about 500 people.
The supplies, which included anaesthetics and cat gut, were brought in overland from Kenya by the German Christoffel Blinden mission.
Dr Jo Lusi, the only surgeon working in Goma, told reporters that a combination of lack of food, water and medicine and the spectre of cholera could spell disaster for the region.
"The food situation is already very, very bad...Nobody has anything to eat and all the roads that were bringing in food are closed," he said.
Cholera is endemic in the region and in 1994 cholera and dysentery killed about 1,000 people daily in Goma after a massive exodus of refugees from Rwanda.
More than a million Rwandans are still in eastern Zaire, caught in a spreading civil war.
"If the cholera begins to do its job, the people will see that the war did not do much," he said.
